text:
emily: Heads up — customer FastPay hit us with a p99 latency complaint. Their p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s around 03:00 UTC. They say it started after our grace-policy rollout yesterday. ticket CS-1289.
raj: saw the alert. correlates with a small change to continuous-batcher grace_window default rolled at 02:45. suspect hold-time tradeoff.
maria: can we get exact pod logs for that tenant? tiny prompts -> long tail is our usual suspect.
jun: grabbing logs now. query: `curl -s http://admin-internal/metrics?tenant=fastpay | jq .batcher` — looks like avg_coalesce_wait jumped to 45ms, p99 coalesce wait 650ms on a handful of pods.
emily: wow 650ms wait alone explains most of it. combined with model startup and kv fetch -> 1.2s.
sre-oncall: attach recent config from rollout:
```
continuous_batcher:
  grace_window_ms: 40   # new default
  min_batch_size: 2
  max_batch_size: 32
  adaptive_coalesce: true
```
raj: previous value was grace_window_ms: 8 (can confirm in git history). The larger window helps throughput but kills tiny-prompt latency.
maria: customer has lots of tiny requests (avg 12 tokens). they fall into tiny-path and wait for grace_window. we should treat tenant as latency-sensitive.
support-bot: CS update: FastPay says it impacts checkout UX. They are on Dedicated with reserved capacity.
jun: reproduction steps (local):
1) run loadgen with many tiny requests (payload 10–20 tokens) at qps ~50
2) enable grace_window 40ms in config
3) observe p95/p99 jump in ~1 min
Commands:
```
python tools/loadgen.py --qps 50 --prompt small.json --tenant fastpay
kubectl logs -l shard=allocator -c batcher | grep coalesce
```
emily: mitigation options:
- roll back grace_window to 8ms for all tenants (fast, blunt)
- set per-tenant override: grace_window_ms: 8 for fastpay (preferred)
- set a soft cap: if observed avg tokens < 20 then reduce grace_window automatically
- route FastPay to non-coalescing path (disable batching) for critical routes
raj: quick hotfix plan: patch tenant override config and rollout to canary pool (2 pods) -> monitor p99. if good, roll to rest.
maria: canary approved. I'll patch config in vault: `redwoodctl tenants set-config fastpay --batcher.grace_window_ms=8`
ops-bot: deploy job queued: rollout/canary/batcher-config-change by maria — started.
jun: monitoring dashboards: adding temporary per-tenant p95/p99 chart and coalesce_wait histogram. hooking alerts to CS-1289.
emily: also add a throttling fallback: if coalesce_wait p99 > 300ms for a tenant, downgrade to immediate dispatch path for that tenant for 5 minutes.
raj: implementation note: immediate dispatch increases cost but keeps UX. add metric for fallback activations.
sre-oncall: timeline and owner: Maria will own hotfix + canary (15m), Raj to validate metrics (ongoing), Jun to run repro (now), Emily to coordinate with CS and update customer (now+).
support-bot: pinged FastPay with ETA ~30m and asked for any specific routes that are most impacted.
emily: after canary looks good, we'll create PR to revert global grace_window change and add per-tenant opt-in flag for larger grace_window.
jun: quick logs from canary (first 5m): coalesce wait p99 dropped to 12ms, overall p99 for FastPay dropped to 140ms. looks promising.
maria: rolling to remaining pods now.
ops-bot: rollout/canary/batcher-config-change -> success on 2/2 pods. initiating gradual rest of pool.
raj: keep an eye on throughput regressions. expected small throughput drop for high-batch workloads — tracking token/sec by model.
emily: note for postmortem: need a test in CI that runs tiny-prompt synthetic workloads when changing grace_window defaults.
sre-oncall: creating incident ticket INF-2026 to track RCA and postmortem.
emily: good catch everyone. I'll keep CS updated and close when p99 stabilizes for 30m.
support-bot: FastPay acknowledged interim fix, appreciates quick response :thumbsup:
